title: Multiple choice — Hydraulic terminology
prompt:
The word hydraulics comes from the Greek word for:
- A. Force
- B. Water
- C. Oil
- D. Motion
answer: B — Water.

title: Short answer — Pascal’s law
prompt: What happens to an applied pressure change in a confined fluid at rest?
answer: The pressure change is transmitted equally and undiminished throughout the fluid and to the container walls.

title: Multiple choice — Static fluid pressure
prompt:
Four open containers hold the same liquid to the same vertical depth. Their shapes and volumes differ. How does the pressure at the bottom compare?
- A. The largest volume produces the highest pressure.
- B. The widest container produces the highest pressure.
- C. All four have the same bottom pressure.
- D. The narrowest container has no bottom pressure.
answer: C — All four have the same bottom pressure. For the same liquid, pressure depends on vertical depth rather than container shape or volume.

title: Multiple choice — Mechanical advantage
prompt:
Which arrangement increases output force in an ideal hydraulic system?
- A. Output piston area larger than input piston area.
- B. Output piston area smaller than input piston area.
- C. Equal input and output piston areas.
- D. Changing the fluid colour.
answer: A — Larger output piston area. It produces greater force at the same pressure, with less output travel for a given input stroke.

title: True or false — Viscosity
prompt:
Mark each statement true or false.
- a. Viscosity is a liquid’s internal resistance to flow.
- b. A liquid that flows slowly generally has high viscosity.
- c. Liquid viscosity increases as temperature decreases.
- d. Every fluid has the same viscosity at 30°F.
- e. Viscosity is another name for pressure.
- f. A Saybolt universal viscosimeter measures viscosity.
answer: a True; b True; c True; d False; e False; f True.

title: Matching — Fluid properties
prompt:
Match each term to its definition.
Term	Definition choices
1. Fire point	A. Ability to resist oxidation and deterioration over time.
2. Chemical stability	B. Temperature at which enough vapour is released to ignite momentarily when a flame is applied.
3. Flash point	C. Temperature at which enough vapour is released to ignite and sustain burning.
answer: 1-C; 2-A; 3-B. Flash point means momentary ignition; fire point means sustained burning.

title: Categorization — Hydraulic fluid types
prompt:
Sort each characteristic into vegetable-base, mineral-base MIL-H-5606, or phosphate-ester fluid such as Skydrol/HyJet.
- a. Blue colour.
- b. Red colour.
- c. Typically light purple.
- d. Castor oil and alcohol base.
- e. Kerosene/petroleum base.
- f. Skydrol is a common example.
- g. Natural rubber seals.
- h. Neoprene seals.
- i. Butyl rubber or ethylene-propylene seals.
- j. Fire-resistant fluid for high-performance aircraft.
- k. Additives help prevent foaming and corrosion.
- l. MIL-H-7644.
answer: Vegetable: a, d, g, l. Mineral MIL-H-5606: b, e, h, k. Phosphate ester: c, f, i, j.

title: Fill in the blank — Compatibility
prompt: MIL-H-83282 is a synthetic hydrocarbon fluid that is backward compatible with MIL-H-________.

title: Multiple choice — Seal compatibility
prompt:
Which seal material is unsuitable for Skydrol according to the presentation?
- A. Butyl rubber.
- B. Ethylene-propylene elastomer.
- C. Neoprene.
- D. Both A and B.
answer: C — Neoprene. The presentation also identifies Buna-N petroleum-fluid seals as incompatible with Skydrol.

title: Multiple answer — Fluid requirements
prompt:
Select all desirable hydraulic-fluid properties.
- A. Low resistance to flow.
- B. Chemical stability.
- C. Good lubrication and corrosion protection.
- D. Compatibility with seals and lines.
- E. Easy compression during normal operation.
- F. A tendency to foam and retain air bubbles.
answer: A, B, C and D. Hydraulic liquid should resist compression and should not foam or retain air bubbles.

title: Short answer — Fluid care
prompt: Give two reasons to keep hydraulic systems and fluid containers sealed. What may happen if incompatible fluid types are mixed?
answer: Sealing helps exclude contamination, air and moisture. Incompatible fluids can swell or damage seals, cause seal breakdown and block the system. Slide 47 specifically identifies 83282 as backward compatible with 5606.

title: Multiple choice — Idle circulation
prompt:
Which system allows fluid to circulate from the reservoir, through the pump and neutral selector valves, and back to the reservoir without maintaining stored operating pressure?
- A. Closed-centre system.
- B. Open-centre system.
- C. A sealed accumulator alone.
- D. A brake deboost system alone.
answer: B — Open-centre system.

title: Categorization — Open and closed centre
prompt:
Assign each description to the open-centre or closed-centre system described in the slides.
- a. Selector valves arranged in series.
- b. Selector valves arranged in parallel.
- c. Fewer components and simpler troubleshooting.
- d. Can store hydraulic energy using an accumulator and check valves.
- e. Neutral selector valves allow circulation back to the reservoir.
- f. Can operate several systems or components at once.
answer: Open centre: a, c, e. Closed centre: b, d, f.

title: Fill in the blanks — Closed-centre operation
prompt: In a closed-centre system, hydraulic fluid flows to the actuators when ________. Hydraulic ________ remains available in the system.
answer: Required / an actuator is commanded; pressure.

title: Multiple choice — Stored hydraulic energy
prompt:
Which arrangement can store hydraulic energy for later use?
- A. Open-centre system with a thermal relief valve only.
- B. Closed-centre system with an accumulator and check valves.
- C. Open reservoir with no pump.
- D. Return filter alone.
answer: B — Closed centre with an accumulator and check valves.

title: Short answer — Power pack
prompt: What is a hydraulic power pack? Name four components listed in the presentation.
answer: A self-contained hydraulic power system. Components: electric pump, pressure control valves, selector valves and reservoir.

title: Diagram identification — Reservoirs
prompt:
Using the reservoir picture in the PDF:
- Identify the reservoir type on the left.
- Identify the reservoir type on the right.
- Which reservoir is in-line?
answer: Left: integral reservoir. Right: in-line reservoir. The right-hand reservoir is separate and connected by tubing or hose.

title: Short answer — Reservoir functions
prompt: Besides storing hydraulic fluid, state two functions of a reservoir.
answer: Any two: purging air, separating contamination, allowing thermal expansion, accommodating changes in system fluid-volume requirements.

title: Short answer — Pressurized reservoirs
prompt: Why are pressurized reservoirs useful on high-altitude aircraft? Name the three pressurizing methods listed in the slides.
answer: Provides a positive fluid supply at the pump inlet and helps prevent foaming. Methods: aspirator, bleed air and hydraulic system pressure/bootstrap.

title: Multiple choice — Early aircraft brakes
prompt:
The early brake system using a rubber expander tube is described as:
- A. An open-centre system.
- B. A closed hydraulic system.
- C. A pneumatic-only system.
- D. An electrical-only system.
answer: B — Closed hydraulic system.

title: Multiple choice — Modern aircraft brakes
prompt:
Which brake type does the presentation identify as the modern aircraft arrangement?
- A. Expander-tube brakes.
- B. Floating disc brakes.
- C. Bicycle rim brakes.
- D. Wooden friction blocks.
answer: B — Floating disc brakes.

title: Matching — Actuators
prompt:
Match each actuator to its description.
Actuator	Description choices
1. Single-acting	A. Hydraulic fluid acts on both sides of the piston.
2. Double-acting	B. Hydraulic fluid acts on one side, with spring and/or nitrogen pressure providing the opposing action.

title: Matching — Pressure-control components
prompt:
Match each component to one function.
Components:
1. Pressure regulator.
2. System pressure relief valve.
3. Thermal relief valve.
4. Pressure reducer.
5. Debooster.
6. Unloading valve.
Functions:
- A. Protects an isolated fluid section from excess pressure caused by heating.
- B. Reduces pressure and increases fluid volume delivered to brake actuators.
- C. Maintains a lower pressure for a component that needs less than main-system pressure.
- D. Controls system pressure within a preset operating range.
- E. Protects against pressure exceeding a limit above normal operating pressure.
- F. Returns excess pump flow to the reservoir once the required system pressure is reached.

title: Short answer — Regulator failure
prompt: If the pressure regulator fails and pressure rises excessively, which component provides overpressure protection?
answer: System pressure relief valve.

title: Diagram matching — Components
prompt:
Identify components 1–5 in the numbered diagram in the PDF.
Word bank: accumulator, reservoir, thermal relief valve, filter, system relief valve.
answer: 1: Thermal relief valve(s). 2: Filter. 3: System relief valve. 4: Accumulator. 5: Reservoir.

title: Diagram identification — System type
prompt:
Using the system diagram in the PDF:
- Identify the system type.
- Are its selector valves in series or parallel?
- Describe the flow path when the selectors are neutral.
answer: Open-centre system; selector valves in series. Fluid travels from reservoir through pump and neutral selector valves, then returns to the reservoir.

title: Visual identification — Fluid samples
prompt:
Using the red and purple samples pictured in the PDF:
- Identify the fluid family represented by each sample.
- Which represents BMS 3-11, Skydrol/HyJet?
- Which represents the fire-resistant fluid used on high-performance aircraft?
answer: Left red sample: mineral-base MIL-H-5606 in this comparison. Right purple sample: phosphate ester, such as Skydrol/HyJet. The right sample represents BMS 3-11 and the fire-resistant fluid. Colour alone cannot identify every specification; 83282 is also red.

title: Matching — Formulas
prompt:
Match each quantity to its formula. Here, P means pressure, and t means time.
Quantity	Formula choices
1. Hydraulic pressure	A. \(W=F\times D\)
2. Hydraulic force	B. \(V=A\times D\)
3. Piston area from force and pressure	C. \(P=F/A\)
4. Circular piston area from radius	D. \(F=P\times A\)
5. Fluid volume displaced	E. \(\mathrm{hp}=(F\times D)/(33{,}000\times t)\), using feet and minutes
6. Work	F. \(A=\pi r^2\)
7. Power	G. \(\mathrm{Power}=(F\times D)/t\)
8. Horsepower	H. \(A=F/P\)
